coverage_gaps: The visible Layer 1B evidence is heavily concentrated in advanced packaging, substrate materials, inspection/metrology, and semiconductor data software; cybersecurity and automation were not adequately expanded into company candidates.
Market-pricing checks were not performed in this Layer 1C merge: market caps, valuation, analyst coverage, short interest, and recent price discovery require later validation.
Several non-US tickers and Japan/Taiwan/Europe candidates have unknown current market-cap buckets because no fresh market-data lookup was supplied in the evidence context.
Substrate and material concentration claims rely on supplied secondary context and should be tested against primary filings, technical documentation, customer disclosures, and industry sources.

The optical interconnect lane has a strong upstream hypothesis around Aixtron, but the downstream public-company mapping for lasers, modules, and transceivers needs direct filing and customer evidence.
AI data-center power and specialized AI cloud capacity are included from supplied context, but current customer contracts, capacity, financing, and revenue exposure require primary-source validation.
No direct ETF or fund mapping was performed; this universe is for single-company research prioritization only.

memory_update.text: For broad Technology research, the best Layer 1 universe should treat AI semiconductors as the demand driver but emphasize second-order bottlenecks in packaging materials, inspection/metrology, photonics tools, data-center power, specialized AI cloud capacity, and semiconductor orchestration software.
Advanced packaging substrate yield, copper/plating chemistry, ABF-style insulating materials, and package inspection/metrology are the highest-priority nodes in the current evidence set.
Compound semiconductor epitaxy tools remain a promising underfollowed AI optical-interconnect node, with Aixtron as the clearest supplied candidate and laser/module suppliers as reference anchors.

Semiconductor manufacturing analytics and orchestration software should stay in the Layer 1 universe because chiplet and advanced-packaging workflows create cross-company yield, traceability, and coordination problems.

Cybersecurity, automation, testing/certification, distributors, and niche software/data beyond semiconductor manufacturing remain under-sourced and require focused Layer 1B searches before final breadth is adequate.

summary: Layer 1C merges the available Layer 1A theme map and visible Layer 1B node outputs into a ranked Serenity initial universe for Technology. The strongest evidence-backed lanes are AI infrastructure chokepoints below obvious chip winners: advanced packaging substrates/materials, copper/plating chemistry, inspection/metrology, semiconductor yield-data software, compound-semiconductor photonics tools, specialized AI cloud capacity, and AI data-center power. The universe deliberately balances reference anchors with underfollowed or second-order names. Because the supplied Layer 1B evidence is deepest for advanced packaging and thin for cybersecurity, automation, and broader software, those areas remain coverage gaps rather than fully populated candidate lanes.
